mainTopic: Why does the תורה need a special verse to exclude an ארוסה (betrothed woman) and a שומרת יבם from the סוטה waters, when a ברייתא already seems to exclude them?
overview: The amud opens with the last item of a list from the earlier ברייתא: the court gives the warning on behalf of a husband who is a שעמום. The גמרא then asks what רבי יאשיה learns from ״תחת אישה״, which רבי יונתן uses to exclude a שומרת יבם. The answer is that רבי יאשיה uses it for a comparison (היקש) between man and woman. Next the גמרא asks why verses are needed at all, since a ברייתא brought by רבי אחא בר חנינא teaches from ״מבלעדי אישך״ that a woman is a סוטה only if her husband was with her before the other man. רמי בר חמא answers that the verse covers a case where the ארוס was with her in her father's house. Applying this to a שומרת יבם runs into רב's ruling that a יבם who was with her makes her his full wife. The גמרא answers that רבי יונתן holds like שמואל, who says the יבם acquires her only for the matters in the תורה's section. Finally, the גמרא shows that רב can explain his view even according to רבי יונתן: the need for a פסוק to exclude her proves she is otherwise a full wife.

steps.title: End of the list: the husband who is mentally ill
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the earlier ברייתא's list: a שעמום, a husband who is mentally unstable, for whom the court gives the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: This single word finishes a list from the previous ברייתא, of husbands who cannot give the warning (קינוי) themselves, so the court does it for them. The list ends here with the שעמום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a שעמום cannot properly warn his wife, the בית דין steps in on his behalf. This closes the earlier teaching, and the גמרא is about to move to a question on רבי יאשיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is mentally unstable or confused

phrases.english: A mentally ill person.
phrases.notes: This is the last item in a list that started on the previous page: husbands for whom the court gives the warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's list from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court gives the warning on behalf of a husband who is a שעמום.

steps.title: What does רבי יאשיה do with ״תחת אישה״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יאשיה uses the words ״תחת אישה״, since he does not use them the way the other opinion does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יאשיה, what does he do with this phrase "under her husband"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יאשיה learns from the words ״תחת אישה״. רבי יונתן uses them to exclude a שומרת יבם, but רבי יאשיה does not exclude her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no words in the תורה are extra. The other opinion uses ״תחת אישה״ for an exclusion. Since רבי יאשיה doesn't use it that way, he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: "Under her husband": a phrase in the סוטה section
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoshiya,
what does he do with this "under her husband"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, הַאי ״תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא's list to the dispute over how to read ״תחת אישה״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יאשיה learns from the phrase ״תחת אישה״.

steps.title: He uses it to compare man and woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה uses ״תחת אישה״ for a היקש, a comparison between the man and the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to compare a man to a woman and a woman to a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יאשיה uses ״תחת אישה״ to make a comparison (היקש) between man and woman. The details come later in the מסכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the phrase is not extra for רבי יאשיה. It teaches a היקש instead of an exclusion. This explains why he doesn't use it to exclude a שומרת יבם, as רבי יונתן does.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
To compare two things so the same law applies to both (היקש)

phrases.english: He needs it to compare
a man to a woman and a woman to a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהַקִּישׁ אִישׁ לְאִשָּׁה וְאִשָּׁה לְאִישׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יאשיה uses ״תחת אישה״ for a היקש comparing man and woman.

steps.title: Why need a verse at all? ״מבלעדי אישך״ already excludes an ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions assume an ארוסה would drink without a special verse. But a ברייתא learns from ״מבלעדי אישך״ that a סוטה must have been with her husband first, which already rules out an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the reason (an ארוסה doesn't drink) is only because these verses are written; otherwise I would say an ארוסה drinks? But when רבי אחא בר חנינא came from the South, he brought a ברייתא: "besides your husband" means only when the husband was with her before the other man, not when the other man was with her before the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole discussion. Why do we need any special verse to exclude an ארוסה, when another ברייתא already excludes her automatically?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions used a verse to exclude an ארוסה, which implies that without it she would drink. But the ברייתא reads ״מבלעדי אישך״ to mean the סוטה law applies only if the husband was with her before the other man. An ארוסה has not yet lived with her husband, so any other man came first, and she should be excluded without an extra verse.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is only because these verses are written
I would have thought
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים)
"Besides your husband" (במדבר 5:20)
The husband's being with her

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether an ארוסה drinks. Everyone agrees she doesn't. The question is why a special verse is needed to teach that, when the ברייתא already excludes her.

phrases.english: But the reason is that these verses are written,
phrases.notes: He means the verses each opinion used to exclude an ארוסה.

phrases.english: but if it were not so,
would I have said a betrothed woman drinks?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא,
phrases.english: But when Rabbi Acha bar Chanina came from the South,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:
"Besides your husband"
means when the husband was with her before the other man,
and not when the other man was with her before the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, טַעְמָא דִּכְתִיבִי הָנֵי קְרָאֵי, הָא לָאו הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲרוּסָה שָׁתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind both opinions, that a verse is needed to exclude an ארוסה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a special verse to exclude an ארוסה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא of ״מבלעדי אישך״ requires the husband to have been with her first. An ארוסה never meets that, so a separate exclusion seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: when the ארוס was with her in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The extra verse is needed for an unusual case: the ארוס was with her while she still lived in her father's house, before the other man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: You find it needed where the betrothed man was with her in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers that there is a case the ברייתא does not cover. The ארוס was with her before the wedding, while she was still at her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case the husband was with her before the other man, so ״מבלעדי אישך״ would not exclude her. That is why a separate verse is needed to teach that an ארוסה still doesn't drink.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (a case where it is needed)
The betrothed man
In her father's house (before the wedding)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the category of ארוסה stays excluded even in the unusual case where the order of events would otherwise make her a סוטה.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
You find it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ אָרוּס בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: where the betrothed man was with her in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a specific case where the special verse is still needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of ״מבלעדי אישך״ makes the verse excluding an ארוסה unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is needed where the ארוס was with her first, in her father's house.

steps.title: Applying the same answer to a שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies רמי בר חמא's answer to the parallel case of a שומרת יבם: the יבם was with her in her father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Correspondingly, regarding a שומרת יבם: where the יבם was with her in her father-in-law's house?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next challenge. The other opinion also excludes a שומרת יבם, so the גמרא asks whether the same kind of case explains the need for that exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the same logic, a separate verse for a שומרת יבם would only be needed if the יבם was with her before the other man. The גמרא proposes that case so it can test it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The matching case, by the same logic
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
Her father-in-law's house

phrases.english: Correspondingly, regarding a widow waiting for her yavam:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ יָבָם בְּבֵית חָמִיהָ.
phrases.english: would it be where the yavam was with her in her father-in-law's house?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רמי בר חמא's answer to the parallel case, setting up a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the parallel case for a שומרת יבם is one where the יבם was with her first.

steps.title: Then she is no longer a שומרת יבם but his full wife
steps.stepSummary: If the יבם was with her, she is no longer a שומרת יבם. רב rules that this acquires her fully as his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do you call her a שומרת יבם? She is his full wife, for רב said: he acquired her for everything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the parallel case. Once the יבם is with her, she is simply his full wife, so it makes no sense to call her a שומרת יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב rules that when a יבם is with the widow, even without meaning it as יבום, he acquires her as his wife in every way. So the case from step 6 is not a שומרת יבם at all. It seems the exclusion of a שומרת יבם cannot be explained the way רמי בר חמא explained ארוסה. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: You call her (by this name)
His full, complete wife
He acquired her for everything

phrases.english: But do you call her a widow waiting for her yavam?
She is his full wife,
for Rav said: he acquired her for everything!
phrases.notes: This means that once the יבם was with her, she counts as his wife for every law, including the laws of סוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the parallel case proposed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רמי בר חמא's kind of case to explain the exclusion of a שומרת יבם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Per רב, a יבם who is with her acquires her fully. So in that case she is no longer a שומרת יבם, and the parallel fails.

steps.title: רבי יונתן holds like שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן holds like שמואל: a יבם who was with his יבמה acquires her only for the matters written in the תורה's section about יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן's view follows שמואל, who said: He acquires her only for the matters stated in the תורה's section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. רבי יונתן holds like שמואל, so the יבם does not acquire her fully as his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that, according to רב, a יבם who was with her makes her his full wife, so she would no longer be a שומרת יבם. שמואל disagrees. He says she is acquired only for the things the תורה's section mentions, such as inheriting the brother and being freed with a גט. So she is still a שומרת יבם. Since the יבם was with her before the other man, ״מבלעדי אישך״ would not exclude her, and רבי יונתן's פסוק is needed to exclude her from drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquired her as a wife
The matters written in the Torah's section about יבום

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not say the יבם acquires nothing. He acquires her in a limited way, only for what the תורה's section of יבום speaks about.

phrases.english: In accordance with Shmuel, who said:
He does not acquire her except
for the matters stated in the passage.
phrases.notes: This is the Torah's section about יבום, דברים 25:5-10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by tying רבי יונתן to שמואל's position instead of רב's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the תנא to a different אמורא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being with her makes her a full wife, as רב says, so she is no longer a שומרת יבם and needs no פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יונתן holds like שמואל. She is acquired only partially, so a פסוק is needed to exclude her from סוטה.

steps.title: Are רב and שמואל just repeating the תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: If so, perhaps רב follows רבי יאשיה and שמואל follows רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say that רב stated his view like רבי יאשיה, and שמואל stated his view like רבי יונתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רב and שמואל is the same as the earlier argument between רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן. This sets up the next step, where the suggestion will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 linked רבי יונתן to שמואל. That would seem to force רב to side with רבי יאשיה, so רב would be against רבי יונתן. The גמרא prefers not to say that an אמורא's view simply depends on a תנאים argument, so it tests this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let us say, a suggestion that is often rejected

phrases.english: If so, let us say
that Rav stated his view like Rabbi Yoshiya
and Shmuel stated his view like Rabbi Yonatan?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out a consequence of step 8's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view, which would now be against רבי יונתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יונתן needs שמואל's view to explain the פסוק, then רב must disagree with רבי יונתן and follow רבי יאשיה.

steps.title: רב's view works even for Rabbi Yonatan
steps.stepSummary: רב can say his view fits רבי יונתן too. The פסוק had to exclude her, which shows she is otherwise a full wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: What I said holds even according to רבי יונתן. Since the verse was needed to exclude her, this shows she is his full-fledged wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of step 9. רב's view does not have to depend on the תנאים argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב turns the פסוק around. If she were not a full wife, no פסוק would be needed to exclude her from the סוטה laws. The fact that the תורה had to exclude her shows she is a full wife in every other way. Only the סוטה law is an exception for her.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you, a defense of someone's view
To exclude her
By inference, it follows that
His full-fledged wife

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק can be read two ways. In שמואל's reading she is still a שומרת יבם and not a full wife, and the פסוק excludes her as a שומרת יבם. In רב's reading she is a full wife, and the פסוק makes an exception for the סוטה law alone. That is why רב fits even רבי יונתן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the argument between רב and שמואל from being just a repeat of the תנאים argument.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
What I said,
holds even according to Rabbi Yonatan.
Since the verse was needed to exclude her,
this implies that she is his full-fledged wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי — אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 9's suggestion that רב must follow רבי יאשיה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב and שמואל simply follow the two תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the exclusion פסוק proves she is not a full wife. It can instead prove the opposite: she is a full wife, and only the סוטה law excludes her.
